answer: The admission bond price rises with the number of new identities per epoch, so a flood of aliases makes each next alias more expensive than the last. Registering a thousand aliases in one epoch means paying the congested price on the last nine hundred, while an honest agent registers in a quiet epoch and pays the base price. The terrace of the design is public, the ocean of stakes makes farming a losing trade, and the forge of honest work is what finally pays.
